Subject: Staged commit proposal + evaluation timing (draft MAP attached)

Alex — attaching a short draft MAP that maps milestones to commits and pricing so we can lock Q1 terms quickly. High-level proposal here so you can comment inline: 

- Evaluation window: 2-week technical POC (staging) starting as soon as we confirm test data access. During eval we recommend a hard cap of 150% of agreed daily baseline to avoid surprise bills.
- Staged commit (months after POC):
  * Month 1 (ramp): commit 100M tokens/mo
  * Month 2: commit moves to 250M tokens/mo
  * Month 3+: steady state 500M tokens/mo
- Pricing (example): commit price = $0.45 per 1k tokens; overage slab: 100%-200% billed at 1.6x commit rate; >200% requires pre-approval (or we apply a negotiated emergency slab).
- Commitment credit: if usage < commit in a billing month, unused commit converts to a 30-day credit pool that can be auto-applied to subsequent month usage during the 3-month ramp.

Questions for you: is a 2-week POC timeline reasonable for your team? Do you want a stricter hard cap during the eval (e.g., 100% vs 150%)? We can also change slabs to absolute token thresholds rather than % if that’s easier for procurement.

Attachment: 20261118_MAP-draft.pdf (application/pdf, 1 page)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if that helps.

— Rachel

Thanks Rachel — quick clarifying questions before we share this with procurement: 

1) Measurement basis: when you say "tokens" is that normalized tokens (OpenAI-style) or your internal tokenization? We need a deterministic billing unit so we can reconcile.
2) Overage timing: is overage calculated per billing month or on a rolling 30-day window? Our finance team prefers per-billing-month accounting.
3) Hard cap during eval: we like the idea of a cap. Can you do a 100% hard cap for the two-week POC and then move to 150% for the first 60 days of ramp? That would give our engineers safety while we tune prompts.
4) Credits: how does the 30-day credit pool work if we hit the second month commit but then dip below in month three? Any expiration?

We’re generally aligned but need the answers above to move to procurement. Also — are you open to a short, firm SLA around latency for the POC? Our product team will want a baseline (95th p50 numbers) in writing.

Alex — great questions. Apologies for the long email, but wanted to make the slab math explicit with a couple of concrete examples so procurement has something to sign off on. Attached is the usage CSV from Rachel for reference.

Measurement unit
- We bill on Redwood-normalized tokens (we publish our tokenizer reference). We will include the same tokenizer code in the contract appendix so both sides can reconcile counts. Billing unit = per 1,000 tokens.

Billing window
- Overage is calculated on a calendar billing month. Rolling windows cause reconciliation headaches for procurement; we’ll stick to calendar months unless otherwise negotiated.

Proposed ramp slabs (applies once the POC completes):
- Tier A (up to commit): $0.45 / 1k tokens
- Tier B (100%–200% of commit): $0.72 / 1k tokens (1.6x commit rate)
- Tier C (>200% of commit): $1.35 / 1k tokens (3.0x), subject to pre-approval for sustained usage above 200%

Examples
- If commit = 500M tokens/mo and actual usage = 600M tokens: charge = (500M * Tier A rate) + (100M * Tier B rate).
- If usage = 1.2B tokens: charge = (500M * Tier A) + (500M * Tier B) + (200M * Tier C at emergency approval rate).

Grace & caps during evaluation
- We can offer: 100% hard cap for the two-week POC (billing cutoff — traffic will be throttled once reached), and a 150% soft cap for the first 60 days of ramp. Soft cap behavior: alerts + a one-time 10% discount on the first overage billing month during the 60-day ramp.

Credits & expiration
- Unused commit converts to a 30-day credit pool; credits auto-apply to the next billing month but expire after three months from issue.

SLA
- We can attach a POC baseline SLA (p50/p95 latency numbers for your region) with a 2-week verification period built into the MAP appendix. 

Attachment: saasco_usage_history.csv (CSV, 3 months)

If this looks good I’ll ask Legal to bake the slabs and caps into the order form language. Laura — any redline concerns?

— Ben
